title: Construct sharp rank-two residual completions and a one-turn bound
body:
Every partial binary symplectic map with residual-form rank two now has a constructive completion within one turn of its rank/nullity lower bound. The exact count is **2r-2 for every nonalternating form**. An explicit radical-lift condition also attains 2r-2 for alternating forms; otherwise the algorithm returns a proved interval [2r-2,2r-1]. All axes stay in the given ambient space and preserve prescribed fixed spectators. This answers part of [Nick Petalas's PR6494 handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19363670).

The [all-size proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9797b952ee174f845f682b1a121600416f5c7bd1/research/rank-two-residual-completion/PROOF.md) reduces alternating rank two to a nonalternating rank-one or rank-two problem with two legal turns. The radical-lift criterion is sufficient, not necessary. Exact closed-case examples need five turns at r3 and attain six at r4. These controls prevent a false classification. The generic algorithm deliberately retains a gap on the latter input, while a separate full-basis certificate proves its six-turn optimum.

Both warning-strict CPython 3.12.13 registered modes pass. The independent matrix interpreter checks all 7,644 rank-two forms at r3/4, including 714 nonalternating forms with zero diagonal, 30,282 prescribed spectators, 64 larger conjugated inputs and 7,108 complete small-group partial-map distances. A meet-in-the-middle certificate checks 8,066 literal words and excludes every four-turn word for the five-turn fixture. All 120 turn omissions, 11 malformed contracts and three actual source corruptions reject. [Receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9797b952ee174f845f682b1a121600416f5c7bd1/research/rank-two-residual-completion/RESULT.json).

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/rank-two-residual-completion
```

All 13 committed package files pass byte/mode and official-export checks. Both read-only, Git-free, empty-PATH replays agree and leave all 14 export files unchanged. Hosted planning and replay passed at the published head: [run 41568764500](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41568764500). The first sealed run exposed read-only permissions copied into a private mutation fixture; the verifier now makes only its temporary test copy writable before corruption. The package inputs stay read-only and the scientific counts are unchanged. Frozen predecessor bytes are included; no pending branch or network is needed. The shallow checkout does not support a full-history ancestry claim. Independent human and proof-kernel acceptance are unclaimed.

This is an **unsigned formal turn tariff**, not Gaussian paid rank, physical cost, native admission or new kappa. The alternating closed case's general optimum remains open. Signed contact binding, absolute phase, monomial passes, dirty restoration, precision, stock, tape, compiler, outer admission and all five selected assumptions remain. Lean, Docker and the selected cold replay were not run.

Only `research/rank-two-residual-completion/` is added. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19364310). Canonical main 7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a, priority 8/selected 6030 remained unchanged at submission. The selected binding example, live handoffs, open PRs and main searches were checked. The residual-form cache covered 463 open PRs and 6,456 Discussion records; sparse local inventory, nested diffs and unpublished work remain limits. New P104 replay/precision and native-binding claims are separate scopes.

Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no subagents. Credit Nick Petalas/6494 for the retained rank-one kernel and proof and 5085 for residual forms/cutoffs; Krzysztof Wojt/5097 for the general lower bound and zero-form algorithm; Brian/JoyboyBrian/5051 for signed compatibility; David Ganz/Dugongue/4841 and the retained native/compiler lineage. Wall forms and symplectic elimination are classical. [David Callan's 1976 paper](https://pages.stat.wisc.edu/~callan/papers/transvections/transvections.pdf) establishes binary exceptional classes; this proof does not import that classification or claim literature priority. No merge, closure or selected-frontier change is requested.
